bug_info.bug_desc: The register TL-UL port's integrity-error output was left unconnected, so an integrity error on the register interface was dropped and never contributed to the bus-integrity-error status, the fatal alert, or local escalation. The memory-bus adapter error was used directly as a scalar condition in the status write-enable, alert request, and escalation logic; with the register-port error added as a second bit, those expressions must OR-reduce the aggregation vector so an error from either TL-UL port is observed. This violated the spec requirement that a bus integrity error on either bus interface must set the bus-integrity-error status, generate a fatal alert, and enter the local escalated state.
bug_info.fix_hint: Connect u_reg_regs.intg_err_o to one bit of the bus_integ_error aggregation vector, keep the SRAM adapter intg_error_o on the other bit, and OR-reduce bus_integ_error in the status write-enable, alert request, and local escalation expressions using |bus_integ_error so that an integrity error from either the register interface or the memory interface is recorded and escalates correctly.
